Reference.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1531 Account Access Removal

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A Windows Active Directory account was deleted (event 4726) or disabled (event 4725). The triage question: is this routine identity lifecycle (HR-driven offboarding, a scripted cleanup) performed by an authorised administrator, or an attacker removing access - cleaning up a throwaway account they created, or disabling a legitimate account to deny availability and slow response?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Deleting or disabling accounts can break access removal audit trails, destroy the primary evidence of an attacker-created identity, or lock defenders and business users out of banking systems during an incident. A burst of deletions/disables by one actor is a hallmark of destructive impact or anti-forensics.

Assets.AssetType: Windows member servers where local accounts are managed

LogSources.LogSource: Windows Security event log - logs-system.security-* (verified live: 4726 and 4725 present with Subject/Target fields populated)

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security "User Account Management" auditing shipped via Elastic Agent to logs-system.security-* (verified live).
winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName (actor) and winlog.event_data.TargetUserName (affected account) populated on 4725/4726 (verified live).

Signal.Name: Account removed
Signal.Details: event.code 4726 (deleted) or 4725 (disabled) on a domain controller. SubjectUserName is the actor; TargetUserName is the account removed; TargetDomainName is the account domain.

Signal.Name: Actor burst
Signal.Details: One SubjectUserName performing many delete/disable operations in a short window indicates mass account tampering rather than a single lifecycle change.

Input.name: $target_user
Input.description: The account that was deleted or disabled (winlog.event_data.TargetUserName from the alert).

Input.name: $actor
Input.description: The user who performed the deletion/disable (winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName from the alert).

ImmediateCapture.Item: Event code from the alert (4726 = deleted, 4725 = disabled) and the DC (host.name)

InitialAssessment.Rule: If $actor is a known IAM/helpdesk offboarding identity AND only $target_user was affected AND the account maps to a departing employee, lean routine lifecycle (False Positive / authorised).

If $actor deleted/disabled MANY accounts in the window, or $target_user was created within the same window (throwaway cleanup), or the actor is a normal user/service account with no admin duty, escalate.

Investigation.Goal: Decide whether the deletion/disabling of $target_user was an authorised lifecycle action or attacker-driven access removal / anti-forensics, and whether it is part of a broader burst.

Step.name: Reconstruct the delete/disable of the target account
Step.Purpose: Confirm what happened to $target_user, who did it, on which DC, and when - the anchor facts for the case.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("4725","4726") AND winlog.event_data.TargetUserName == "$target_user" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL action = CASE(event.code=="4726","account-deleted", event.code=="4725","account-disabled", event.code) | STATS events = COUNT(*), first_seen = MIN(@timestamp), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp), actors = VALUES(winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName), dcs = VALUES(host.name), domains = VALUES(winlog.event_data.TargetDomainName) BY action | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: A single action by a recognised admin identity is routine. Multiple actors, or an actor that is not an administrator, is suspicious. Record first_seen/last_seen to align with the actor-burst window in INV-02.

Step.name: Profile the actor's account-management activity
Step.Purpose: Distinguish a one-off lifecycle change from mass account tampering: how many accounts did $actor create, enable, disable, delete, reset, or re-group in the window.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName == "$actor" AND event.code IN ("4720","4722","4723","4724","4725","4726","4738","4740","4767","4728","4732","4756") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL op = CASE(event.code=="4720","create",event.code=="4722","enable",event.code=="4725","disable",event.code=="4726","delete",event.code=="4740","lockout",event.code=="4767","unlock",event.code=="4728","group-add-global",event.code=="4732","group-add-local",event.code=="4756","group-add-universal",event.code=="4724","pw-reset",event.code=="4738","account-change",event.code) | STATS n = COUNT(*), targets = COUNT_DISTINCT(winlog.event_data.TargetUserName), sample_targets = VALUES(winlog.event_data.TargetUserName) BY op | SORT n DESC | LIMIT 25
Step.AnalystNotes: A single delete/disable with no other operations is consistent with offboarding. Many deletes/disables across many distinct targets = destructive impact or clean-up. Note if the SAME actor recently created accounts (4720) then deleted them - attacker throwaway lifecycle.

Step.name: Establish whether the removed account was live and legitimate
Step.Purpose: Separate the removal of a real, actively-used identity (business/availability impact) from the removal of a freshly-created throwaway (attacker anti-forensics).
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours AND winlog.event_data.TargetUserName == "$target_user" AND event.code IN ("4624","4625","4720","4722","4738") | EVAL ev = CASE(event.code=="4624","logon-success",event.code=="4625","logon-fail",event.code=="4720","created",event.code=="4722","enabled",event.code=="4738","changed",event.code) | STATS n = COUNT(*), first_seen = MIN(@timestamp), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp), src_ips = VALUES(source.ip), hosts = VALUES(host.name) BY ev | SORT last_seen DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: A "created" event for $target_user inside the same 4h window as its deletion is a strong attacker signal (create-use-delete). Recent logon-success from unusual source IPs before deletion suggests the account was used maliciously and then removed to hide it. No prior activity at all = likely a stale/never-used account being cleaned up.

Node.Condition: INV-02 shows $actor deleted/disabled MANY distinct accounts in the window, OR INV-03 shows $target_user was created (4720) inside the same window it was removed (create-use-delete), OR the actor is not an authorised administrator.
Node.Result: True Positive (Attacker access removal / anti-forensics - escalate to IR)

Node.Condition: INV-03 shows $target_user had recent logon-success from unusual source IPs shortly before removal AND the actor cannot be tied to an approved offboarding process.
Node.Result: True Positive (Compromised account removed to hide activity - escalate to IR)

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows a single removal by a recognised IAM/helpdesk identity, INV-02 shows no burst, and $target_user maps to a documented leaver / approved offboarding or decommission ticket.
A scripted/scheduled cleanup job (stale-account reaper) with a change record performed the disable/delete and INV-02 breadth matches its documented scope.
Node.Result: Misconfiguration (Over-broad or mistimed automation - fix the job, do not exception blindly)

Node.Condition: Actor identity or the business justification for $target_user cannot be established from IAM/CMDB/ticketing, or breadth is borderline.

FalsePositive.Definition: An authorised administrator or approved automation removed the account as part of documented identity lifecycle (offboarding, decommission, stale-account cleanup).

Indicators.Item: $actor is a known IAM/helpdesk/admin identity acting within its role.
A single account affected, matching an HR leaver or decommission ticket.
No actor burst in INV-02 and no create-use-delete pattern in INV-03.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the offboarding/decommission ticket and the actor's authorisation.
Close as false_positive; if a recurring automation account trips the rule, propose a scoped exception for that actor only.

TruePositive.Definition: An adversary removed access - deleting a throwaway identity to erase evidence, or disabling/deleting a real account to deny availability or slow response.

Indicators.Item: Actor burst: many delete/disable operations across distinct accounts (INV-02).
Actor is not an authorised administrator, or acted outside change windows.

SOCAction.Item: Open an incident; treat the actor identity ($actor) as potentially compromised.
Preserve DC security logs and, where possible, AD object tombstones/backups for the removed accounts.
Hunt for what the actor did before the removals (logons, privilege changes, data access).

Misconfiguration.Definition: An internal automation or admin script removed accounts too broadly or at the wrong time - operationally driven, not malicious.

Indicators.Item: A service/automation account performed the operations on a schedule.
Breadth matches a known cleanup job but caught accounts it should not have.

SOCAction.Item: Engage the automation owner to correct scope/timing; restore any wrongly-removed accounts.
Track under identity-hygiene; do not blanket-exception the rule.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm scope from INV-02: is this one removal or a burst? A burst is an active-incident trigger.
Verify $actor's authorisation with IAM; if unauthorised, disable $actor and revoke its sessions.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: For attacker-driven removals, reconstruct the actor's full activity timeline and contain the source host/identity.
Restore legitimately-needed accounts from AD tombstone/backup; document what was removed.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Review who holds account-deletion rights; tighten delegation to IAM roles only.
Alert on bursts of 4725/4726 by a single actor as a higher-severity correlated analytic.

Escalation.Trigger: Actor-burst removals, create-use-delete pattern, removal of a privileged/active account, or unverifiable actor authorisation.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Offboarding/decommission ticket verified and matches $target_user and $actor.
No actor burst and no create-use-delete pattern.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Actor identity contained and full activity timeline reconstructed.
Wrongly-removed accounts restored; evidence preserved; incident documented.
